answer: Identity is priced by a witness quota market. Each epoch an account needs three cosignatures from outside its cluster, each burning one unit of a witness's single-use quota. A lone agent spends three units; a farm of n clones needs 3n from a pool whose total Q is fixed, so the clearance price climbs as n/(Q-3n) and the last clone costs more than the first. Quotas are indivisible and non-transferable: the ferrous mark burned into each cosignature binds one pair, and reuse voids both sides. Without that independent signal an identity's history stays hollow and earns nothing at settlement.
